C. High level of urban employment with growing real income

Final_2020.explanation: During the Derg regime, the economy was stagnant, and urban centers did not offer high employment or growing real incomes. Had such economic opportunities existed, they would have catalyzed rural-to-urban migration rather than suppressed it.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 40. Which one of the following soils is commonly found in coffee producing areas of Ethiopia? (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: Nitosols are deep, well-drained, reddish-brown tropical soils found extensively in the moist western and southwestern highlands. Their excellent physical properties and nutrient retention make them the prime soils for Ethiopia's robust coffee cultivation.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 41. The form of geographical human mobility involving a permanent or semi-permanent change of residence between clearly defined geographic units is termed as _______________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: Migration is strictly defined in demography as the movement of people across a specified boundary for the purpose of establishing a new or semi-permanent residence.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 42. A census undertaking approach where each individual is recorded in accordance to his/her usual place of residence is called _____________________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: A 'de jure' (by law/right) census counts people according to their legal or usual place of residence, regardless of where they happen to be on census night. This contrasts with a 'de facto' census, which counts them exactly where they are found.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 43. _______________ is the instant of time when the sun strikes the plane of the Earth's equator. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: An equinox occurs twice a year (around March 21 and September 23) when the Earth's axis is inclined neither toward nor away from the sun, resulting in the sun being exactly overhead at the equator.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 44. _______________ refers to the average number of children that a woman would have at the end of her reproductive period if the current age-specific fertility rate remains unchanged. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is a synthetic demographic metric. It estimates the average number of children a hypothetical cohort of women would have if they experienced the current age-specific fertility rates throughout their entire childbearing years (15-49).

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 45. The threshold population number that Ethiopia uses to classify settlements as urban settlement is _______________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: The Ethiopian Central Statistical Agency (CSA) functionally defines an urban center as any locality with a population of 2,000 or more inhabitants, or any administrative capital of a wereda.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 46. The most navigable river in Ethiopia is _______________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: While most Ethiopian rivers flow through steep, unnavigable gorges, the Baro River is the exception. As it reaches the flat Gambela lowlands, it becomes wide and slow enough to support riverine transport.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 47. The endemic large herbivorous mammal found only in the Bale Mountains is _______________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: The Mountain Nyala (Tragelaphus buxtoni) is a flagship endemic antelope species strictly confined to the high-altitude afro-alpine and woodland habitats of southeastern Ethiopia, notably within the Bale Mountains National Park.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 48. The physical soil conservation measure that has been practiced for generations by Konso people of Ethiopia is _______________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: The Konso people are globally renowned for their intricate, centuries-old dry stone agricultural terracing systems. This physical conservation technique allows them to successfully farm steep hillsides while minimizing soil erosion.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 49. A monolithic rock-hewn church in Ethiopia recognized as the 8th wonders of the world registered by the UNESCO is _______________. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: The 11 rock-hewn monolithic churches of Lalibela, carved directly downward into the solid red volcanic tuff of the Lasta massif, are UNESCO World Heritage sites often colloquially referred to as the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 50. _______________ language families are spoken in the western lowlands of Ethiopia along the border with Sudan. (2020)
Final_2020.explanation: The Nilo-Saharan language family (which includes Gumuz, Berta, Anuak, and Nuer) is predominantly spoken by the indigenous communities inhabiting the hot western peripheral lowlands of Ethiopia, bordering South Sudan and Sudan.

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 51. Crude Birth Rate (CBR) (2020)
Final_2020.explanation:
Crude Birth Rate is calculated as total live births divided by total population, multiplied by 1000. Total population = Male (50,000,000) + Female (51,000,000) = 101,000,000. 
\[ CBR = \frac{2,000,000}{101,000,000} \times 1000 \approx 19.8 \]

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 52. Crude Death Rate (CDR) (2020)
Final_2020.explanation:
Crude Death Rate is calculated as total deaths divided by the total population, multiplied by 1000. 
\[ CDR = \frac{800,000}{101,000,000} \times 1000 \approx 7.92 \]

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 53. Rate of natural increase (RNI) (2020)
Final_2020.explanation:
The Rate of Natural Increase is the difference between the Crude Birth Rate and Crude Death Rate divided by 10 to yield a percentage. 
\[ RNI = \frac{19.8 - 7.92}{10} = 1.188\% \]

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 54. General Fertility Rate(GFR) (2020)
Final_2020.explanation:
The General Fertility Rate is calculated as total live births divided by the population of women of reproductive age (15-49 years), multiplied by 1000. 
\[ GFR = \frac{2,000,000}{15,000,000} \times 1000 \approx 133.33 \]

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 55. Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) (2020)
Final_2020.explanation:
Infant Mortality Rate compares the number of deaths of infants under one year old to the total number of live births, multiplied by 1000. 
\[ IMR = \frac{100,000}{2,000,000} \times 1000 = 50 \]

Final_2020.subject: Geography
Final_2020.text: 56. Crude Density (2020)
Final_2020.explanation:
Crude density measures the average spatial distribution of a population, calculated as total population divided by total land area. 
\[ \text{Crude Density} = \frac{101,000,000}{1,000,000} = 101 \text{ persons per } km^2 \]

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 1. With regard to soil erosion in Ethiopia what generalization can be made? (2023)

options.text: A. Ethiopian highlands have been seriously affected by soil erosion
B. Water erosion is the main cause of soil erosion in lowlands of Ethiopia
C. Wind erosion is a dominant type of erosion in the highlands Ethiopia
D. There is a minor problem of soil erosion in the highlands of Ethiopia

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Ethiopian highlands are severely affected by soil erosion primarily due to rugged topography, steep slopes, heavy summer rainfall, and intensive deforestation for agriculture. Water erosion, not wind erosion, is the dominant factor in the highlands.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 2. Which one of the following activities is not part of the tertiary economic sector? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Spinning and weaving involve the processing of raw materials into finished goods, which classifies them as secondary economic activities (manufacturing). Education, health, banking, and insurance are all service-based activities belonging to the tertiary sector.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 3. What is the name of the wind which has strong influence in the summer rains of Ethiopia? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The summer rains (Kiremt) in Ethiopia are primarily brought by the Equatorial westerlies (also known as the Guinea Monsoon), which originate from the Atlantic Ocean and the Congo Basin, bringing heavy moisture to the western and central highlands.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 4. What factors are responsible for Ethiopia to experience low temperature during summer season contrary to other tropical regions? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: During the summer (Kiremt) season, Ethiopia experiences relatively low temperatures primarily due to its high altitude and the heavy, continuous cloud cover that blocks incoming solar radiation.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 5. With reference to the position of the sun at various latitudes, which one of the following statements is true? (2023)

options.text: A. On June 21 the sun will be directly overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn.
B. The sun is directly overhead at the equator during March and September.
C. On December 22 the sun will be directly overhead at Tropic of Cancer.
D. The sun is directly overhead in the middle and high latitudes during summer solstice.

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The sun is directly overhead at the equator twice a year during the equinoxes, which occur around March 21 and September 23. It is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer on June 21 and the Tropic of Capricorn on December 22.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 6. One of the following is among the human causes of climate change (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Urbanization involves land-use changes, deforestation, and increased greenhouse gas emissions from human activities, making it an anthropogenic (human-induced) cause of climate change. Continental drift, ocean currents, and volcanoes are natural phenomena.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 7. With regard to the spatio-temporal variation of temperature in Ethiopia, what generalization can be made? (2023)

options.text: A. Annual temperature range is greater than diurnal ranges.
B. Hottest months of the year in the central highlands are experienced in spring.
C. Daily temperature range is low in the lowlands compared to the highlands
D. Highest temperatures are recorded in the Danakil Depression in winter

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: In the central highlands of Ethiopia, the hottest months generally occur during the spring season (Belg, from March to May) just before the heavy summer rains bring significant cloud cover and cooler temperatures. Furthermore, diurnal temperature ranges in Ethiopia are generally greater than annual ranges due to its tropical location.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 8. An activity where a family produces only enough to be self-sufficient (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Subsistence farming is an agricultural practice where farmers grow crops and raise livestock primarily to feed themselves and their families, with little to no surplus for commercial sale.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 9. Which of the following drainage system is the largest in terms of annual water discharge? (2023)

options.text: C. The Rift Valley Drainage System

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Western Drainage System, which includes major river basins like the Abay (Blue Nile), Baro-Akobo, and Tekeze, accounts for the vast majority (about 80-84%) of Ethiopia's total annual surface water discharge.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 10. As opposed to declining death rates, birth rates have remained high in rural Ethiopia due to (2023)

options.text: C. Effective utilization of family planning methods.
D. the attitude of rural families towards large number of children

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: High birth rates in rural Ethiopia are heavily influenced by socio-cultural factors, particularly the value placed on having a large number of children for agricultural labor, social security, and traditional prestige. The other options would typically lead to a reduction in birth rates.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 11. Which one of the following identifies the western lowlands of Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: A. Tekeze-Setit, Abay-Dinder and Baro-Akobo lowlands
B. Borana, Wabi Shebele-Ghenale and Ogaden lowlands
C. Wabi Shebele, Ghenale and Borana lowlands
D. Awash, rift valley and Afar lowlands

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The western lowlands stretch along the border with Sudan and South Sudan, encompassing the lower basins of westward-flowing rivers such as the Tekeze-Setit, Abay-Dinder, and Baro-Akobo.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 12. Which of the following is a non-biological factor of population change? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Population change is driven by three main factors: fertility, mortality, and migration. Fertility and mortality are vital (biological) events, whereas migration is a non-biological, spatial movement of people.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 13. Related to the success stories of environmental recovery in sloping areas of Ethiopia such as Konso, which land management strategy is effective in minimizing land degradation? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Konso landscape in southern Ethiopia is globally renowned for its extensive indigenous stone terracing systems. This physical land management strategy effectively minimizes soil erosion and land degradation on steep slopes.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 14. One of the characteristics of a population census is simultaneity. What does simultaneity refer to in this context? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Simultaneity in a population census means that the enumeration should occur over a very limited time frame with reference to a well-defined point in time (the census night), ensuring a snapshot of the population without double counting or omissions due to movement.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 15. One of the following factors is the basis for classifying settlements in to rural and urban (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The primary basis for classifying a settlement as rural or urban is the dominant type of economic activity. Rural settlements are primarily engaged in primary activities like agriculture, while urban settlements are dominated by secondary and tertiary activities like manufacturing and services.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 16. One of the following is a secondary economic activity (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Secondary economic activities involve processing, manufacturing, and construction. Farming and mining extract natural resources (primary), while retailing provides services (tertiary).

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 17. Which of the following is among the characteristics of the Ethiopian industry? (2023)

options.text: A. The industrial sector of Ethiopia is highly advanced
B. Manufacturing is the most important sector in terms of employment generation
C. Ethiopian industries are dominated by heavy manufacturing factories
D. Ethiopia has one of the least developed industrial sectors in the world

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Despite recent growth, Ethiopia's industrial sector historically remains one of the least developed globally, characterized by light manufacturing, agro-processing, and a relatively small contribution to national employment compared to agriculture.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 18. Of the following modes of transport which one provides door to door service? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Road transport is uniquely flexible as vehicles can easily access individual homes, businesses, and specific delivery points, providing direct door-to-door service that air, water, and rail transport cannot achieve due to their reliance on fixed terminals.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 19. Among the following major river basins of western drainage system, which one does not discharge in to the sea through Nile River? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Ghibe (Omo) River belongs to the Inland (Rift Valley) Drainage System, not the Western system, and it empties into Lake Turkana, meaning it has no outlet to the sea. The Baro-Akobo, Tekeze, and Abay all eventually join the Nile system flowing to the Mediterranean Sea.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 20. Concerning urbanization in Ethiopia which one of the following statements is correct? (2023)

options.text: A. Urban growth rates in Ethiopia are very high
B. Ethiopia has an advanced urban system
C. The pace of urbanization is slowing down in Ethiopia
D. Ethiopia has high urbanization level

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Ethiopia has a low overall level of urbanization (a small percentage of the total population lives in urban areas), but the rate at which its urban population is growing is among the highest in the world, driven by heavy rural-to-urban migration.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 21. The Rift Valley Drainage system is characterized by the following in that (2023)

options.text: A. It has northward flow direction
B. The rivers have closed system (have no sea out let)
C. It has the largest catchment area
D. It shows very low fluctuations of water

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Rift Valley drainage system consists primarily of internal (endorheic) basins where rivers terminate in lakes (such as Lake Turkana or the central Rift Valley lakes) and do not have an outlet to any ocean or sea.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 22. The following are the general characteristic of Ethiopian Rivers except: (2023)

options.text: A. Most of them are suitable for navigations
B. They have rapids and waterfalls along their courses
C. They show extreme seasonal fluctuation
D. Most of them have trans-boundary natures

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Most Ethiopian rivers flow across rugged, mountainous terrain, creating steep gradients, rapids, and waterfalls. Combined with high seasonal volume fluctuations, these characteristics make them generally unsuitable for navigation. The Baro River is a rare exception.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 23. Among agro-ecological zones, which one is highly suitable for majority of cereal crops grown in Ethiopia? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Weyna Dega (temperate or middle altitude) zone is characterized by moderate temperatures and adequate rainfall, making it the most suitable agro-ecological zone for growing a wide variety of dominant cereal crops like teff, wheat, and maize.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 24. Which one of the following is man-made lake in Ethiopia ? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Lake Koka (also known as the Koka Reservoir) is an artificial, man-made lake created by the construction of the Koka Dam across the Awash River for hydroelectric power generation.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 25. The Ethiopian lakes are said to be the results of structural activity. This is proved by their (2023)

options.text: D. having less volume of water

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The majority of Ethiopia's lakes lie within the East African Rift Valley, a structurally formed down-faulted graben. Because the Rift Valley floor sits at lower elevations bounded by highlands, it creates a rain shadow effect, resulting in generally dry climatic conditions for the region hosting these structurally-formed lakes.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 26. Among climate change responses, which one is categorized under major adaptation strategies? (2023)

options.text: C. Absorb stresses and maintain function
D. Increase the use of renewable energy

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Adaptation strategies involve adjusting physical and social systems to minimize the negative impacts of climate changes that are already occurring (e.g., building flood defenses). Energy efficiency and renewable energy are mitigation strategies aimed at preventing further climate change.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 27. Which tourist attraction area in Ethiopia is known for the endemic animals? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Bale Mountains National Park is globally renowned for its high levels of endemism. It is a vital sanctuary for several endemic species, most notably the Ethiopian wolf and the mountain nyala.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 28. One of the following Soils of Ethiopia becomes very sticky during wet seasons and cracks severely during dry seasons there by difficult to manage. (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Vertisols are heavy clay soils characterized by a high content of expansible clay minerals. They swell and become highly sticky when wet, and shrink to form deep, wide cracks during dry periods, making agricultural management difficult.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 29. Which of the following is NOT among the main challenges of natural vegetation conservation in Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: A. Adopting alternative source of energy for household consumption

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Adopting alternative sources of energy reduces reliance on fuelwood and charcoal, thereby supporting the conservation of natural vegetation. In contrast, overgrazing, human settlement expansion, and mineral extraction are active challenges causing deforestation.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 30. The least abundant in atmosphere but by far more active greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide is (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) exist in trace amounts (least abundant compared to gases like CO2, methane, or water vapor) but have a remarkably high Global Warming Potential—often thousands of times more active at trapping heat per molecule than carbon dioxide.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 31. The majority of Ethiopian regions receive rainfall during summer season EXCEPT: (2023)

options.text: A. Lowlands in Afar and Southeast

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Most of Ethiopia is dominated by summer (Kiremt) rains. However, the southeastern lowlands receive bi-modal rainfall mainly in spring and autumn, and the Afar lowlands similarly remain largely dry during the Kiremt season.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 32. Which of the following indicators measures the total number of births occurring in a given year per 1000 population? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Crude Birth Rate (CBR) is calculated as the number of live births in a specific year divided by the total mid-year population, expressed per 1,000 individuals.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 33. A type of soil whose mineralogy doesn't show resemblance with the rock beneath over which it rests is (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Fluvisols are azonal, transported soils formed by recent alluvial deposits along rivers and floodplains. Because they are transported by water from other locations, their mineral composition does not generally reflect the underlying bedrock.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 34. Inland water transport, in Ethiopia is limited because of the following except: (2023)

options.text: B. seasonal fluctuation of the volume of rivers
C. the plain nature of the landscape on which the rivers flow
D. presence of rapids and falls along the course of most rivers

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Ethiopia's landscape is predominantly rugged and mountainous, not plains. The rugged topography creates steep gradients, rapids, and waterfalls, which, along with seasonal variations in volume, severely limit inland water navigation.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 35. Which one of the following factors does not contribute to the low level of development of fishery in Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: A. Low eating habit of the majority of the population
B. The long distance of the fishing ground from major settlement areas
D. Availability of high plankton levels

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: High plankton levels support fish populations and would be an advantage for the fishery sector, not a hindrance. The low development of fisheries is largely due to cultural dietary habits, distance to markets, and inadequate technology.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 36. Which one of the following is not the basic and general characteristics of Agriculture in Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: C. Fragmentation of farm plots and Small size of Holdings

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Ethiopian agriculture is overwhelmingly characterized by dependence on rain-fed farming rather than irrigation. The other options (subsistence orientation, small fragmented plots, low input use, and high vulnerability to climate shocks) are defining features of the sector.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 37. If region "A" has crude density of 500 persons per KM2 and its total area is 15,000 KM2, population of the region is (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Crude population density is calculated as Total Population divided by Total Area. Therefore, Population = Density × Area = \( 500 \times 15,000 = 7,500,000 \).

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 38. Which of the following minerals have been produced in Ethiopia since ancient times? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Gold mining (placer gold) and rock salt extraction from the Danakil Depression have been prominent traditional and commercial economic activities in Ethiopia dating back to ancient civilizations.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 39. Which one of the following is the largest river both in volumetric discharge and coverage in the Western Drainage System? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Abay River (Blue Nile) is by far the largest river basin in Ethiopia in terms of both catchment area (coverage) and annual surface water discharge, contributing the lion's share of water to the Western Drainage System.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 40. Which one of the following is not chemical characteristic of a soil? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Porosity relates to the physical arrangement of soil particles and the pore spaces between them, making it a physical characteristic of soil. Soil pH, mineral availability, and electrical conductivity reflect the soil's chemical composition and reactions.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 41. Red sea escarpments and some parts of the Afar region receive rain during winter season as a result of (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: During the winter season (Bega), northeast trade winds blow over the Red Sea picking up moisture. When they hit the Red Sea escarpments and adjacent Afar region, they cause orographic lifting, resulting in winter rains in these specific areas.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 42. Which one is False about population distribution of Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: A. It increases with an increasing altitude
B. Highlands are densely settled than lowlands
C. The proportion of urban population is increasing from time to time
D. There is even population distribution among the regional states

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Ethiopia's population is highly unevenly distributed. The vast majority of the population lives in the highlands due to a favorable climate and better agricultural conditions, while the extensive lowland areas remain sparsely populated.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 43. If the population of towns is grow at the rate which is less than the rate of natural increase (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: In demographic geography, a declining town is characterized by an overall growth rate that falls below its rate of natural increase. This discrepancy indicates that more people are emigrating out of the town than migrating into it (net out-migration).

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 44. Which type of farming system supports the fewest people in Ethiopia? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Shifting cultivation involves clearing plots of forest, farming them briefly, and abandoning them to regenerate. Because it requires immense land areas per person to sustain long fallow periods, it supports the lowest population density among farming systems in Ethiopia, mostly practiced in western peripheral lowlands.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 45. Which of the following is the dominant species of Afro-alpine vegetation? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Giant Lobelia (Lobelia rhynchopetalum) is an iconic, endemic species that characterizes the harsh, high-altitude environments of Ethiopia's Afro-alpine vegetation zone, typically found above 3,200 meters.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 46. Which one of the following drainage basins drains the Amhara, Oromia & Benishangul Gumuz regional states? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Abay (Blue Nile) basin originates in the Amhara region (Lake Tana), carves deep gorges bordering the Oromia region, and continues westward through the Benishangul-Gumuz region before entering Sudan.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 47. A population pyramid can show population distribution by (2023)

options.text: A. Age group and death rate
D. Age group and growth rate

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: A population pyramid is a standard demographic graphing tool that visually breaks down a given population distribution along two distinct variables: age groups (usually in 5-year cohorts) and biological sex (males vs. females).

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 48. The most densely populated part of Ethiopia is (2023)

options.text: A. The north central highlands of Gojjam and Gondar
B. The southwestern coffee growing areas of the country
C. The enset-growing regions of Southern Ethiopia
D. The Cereal-growing regions of Bale and Arsi
E. Awash valley and its surrounding lowlands

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The enset-growing regions of Southern Ethiopia (e.g., Sidama, Gedeo, Gurage zones) support the highest population densities in the country because enset is an extremely high-yielding and drought-resistant staple crop capable of sustaining large numbers of people on very small plots of land.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 49. The ratio between total population and arable part of a country is (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Physiological density is defined as the number of people per unit of agriculturally productive (arable) land. This metric offers a clearer picture of the pressure placed on a country's food-producing resources than crude density.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 50. One of the following demographic measure helps to estimate the average number of children that a woman would have at the end of her reproductive period: (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) measures the average number of children a hypothetical cohort of women would have by the end of their reproductive years if they experienced the current age-specific fertility rates throughout their lives.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 51. Which one of the following areas of is grouped under winter rainfall regions of Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: B. Afar region and red sea escarpments

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: While most of Ethiopia undergoes a dry season during winter (Bega), the Red Sea escarpments and adjacent parts of the Afar region uniquely receive rainfall from moisture-laden northeast trade winds passing over the Red Sea.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 52. The ago-ecological zone that consists of most of the agricultural lands in Ethiopia is: (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Woyna-Dega zone (middle altitudes) offers an optimal temperate climate that supports a vast array of crops, making it the most intensely cultivated agro-ecological zone and host to the majority of Ethiopia's agricultural lands.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 53. Which one of the following regions has the largest population density in Ethiopia? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Southern region (incorporating SNNPR and recently formed states like Sidama) maintains the highest population density among major Ethiopian regions, largely due to fertile highlands and the highly productive enset farming system.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 54. Which one of the following cities is not grouped under secondary cities? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: In Ethiopian urban hierarchy, Addis Ababa is the primary (primate) city, while major regional hubs and chartered cities like Dire Dawa, Bahir Dar, Jimma, and Jigjiga operate as secondary cities. Nekemt is generally categorized as a lower-tier (tertiary) administrative or zonal center.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 55. One of the following is a best example of declining Towns in Ethiopia (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Goba is frequently cited in Ethiopian geography as a classic example of a declining town. It experienced economic and demographic stagnation or decline following the transfer of administrative functions (as a zonal capital) to the rapidly growing nearby town of Robe.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 56. Identify the odd one from the following lakes (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Lake Koka is the odd one out because it is an artificial (man-made) reservoir created for hydroelectric power, whereas Tana, Shalla, Ziway, and Hayk are all naturally formed lakes.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 57. Which one of the following rivers of Ethiopia is found to be navigable river? (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Baro River is the only commercially navigable river in Ethiopia. Due to a gentler gradient in its lower course over the Gambella plains, it provides a navigable water route reaching up to the White Nile system during the rainy season.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 58. All of the following are endemic animals in Ethiopia except: (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: While lions are present in Ethiopia, they are widespread across much of sub-Saharan Africa and are not endemic. The Gelada baboon, Walia ibex, Mountain Nyala, and Simien fox (Ethiopian wolf) are unique species found exclusively in Ethiopia.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 59. Which among the following is not a characteristics of the Ethiopian Lowlands? (2023)

options.text: A. Nomadic and Semi-nomadic with transhumance practices;
B. High prevalence of tropical vector diseases;
C. High temperature and low rainfall;
D. Vast plains that offer a potential for irrigated agriculture;

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Options A, B, C, and D are all accurate descriptions of the Ethiopian lowlands. They are characterized by hot, dry climates, nomadic pastoralism, tropical diseases (like malaria), and vast plains suitable for large-scale irrigation, making 'None of the above' the correct choice.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 60. Which one of the following is not true of the population of Ethiopia? (2023)

options.text: A. Ethiopia has a youthful population
B. Life expectancy at birth is showing a declining trend in Ethiopia
C. Urban areas have lower birth & death rates compared to rural areas.
D. Though declining, fertility and mortality rates are still high in Ethiopia

AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Due to extensive expansions in healthcare access, disease control, and child immunization programs over recent decades, life expectancy at birth in Ethiopia has actually shown a consistent increasing trend, rendering option B false.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 61. During autumn, winds from Indian ocean that shower the southeastern lowlands of Ethiopia are _______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: During the autumn months, south-easterly winds originating from the Indian Ocean blow towards the interior, supplying significant moisture and secondary seasonal rains to the south and south-eastern lowlands of Ethiopia.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 62. A band of low pressure cell around the Earth which generally lies near to the equator where the Northeast Trade winds and Equatorial Westerlies meet/converge is _______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a dynamic, low-pressure belt near the equator where major trade winds from the northern and southern hemispheres converge, heavily influencing seasonal rainfall patterns in tropical regions like Ethiopia.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 63. A system of continuous, compulsory and legal recording of the occurrence and the characteristics of vital events is termed as _______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Vital registration (or civil registration) is the formal governmental process of tracking critical demographic occurrences, continuously capturing data on births, deaths, marriages, and divorces as they occur.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 64. The best soil type used for the cultivation of coffee in Ethiopia is _______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Nitosols are deep, well-drained, red tropical soils rich in nutrients and iron. Their excellent physical properties and moisture-retention capacities make them perfectly suited for the cultivation of highland crops, particularly Arabica coffee.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 65. Permanent or semi-permanent change of residence between clearly defined geographic units is called_______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Migration is fundamentally defined in demography as the spatial mobility of populations involving a permanent or semi-permanent relocation across recognized geographic boundaries.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 66. The national park in Ethiopia known for the predominance of bird species such as pelicans and flamingoes is _______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: Abijatta-Shalla National Park, situated in the Great Rift Valley, centers around two major lakes that provide critical feeding grounds for enormous flocks of aquatic birds, famously serving as a prime habitat for both greater and lesser flamingos as well as great white pelicans.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 67. Afar lowlands and the red sea escarpment areas receive winter rainfall from _______________ winds (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The winter season in Ethiopia is broadly dry except for specific zones like the Red Sea escarpment and bordering Afar lowlands, which receive orographic rainfall from moisture-bearing northeasterly trade winds blowing off the Red Sea.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 68. _______________ is the average rate at which temperature changes per unit of altitudinal change. (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: The lapse rate (or environmental lapse rate) describes how atmospheric temperature decreases as altitude increases in the troposphere. In standard environments, this reduction happens at an average rate of about 6.5°C per 1,000 meters of elevation.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 69. The instant of time when the sun strikes the plane of the Earth's equator & where the length of day and night are equal is called: _______________ (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: An equinox happens twice a year when the tilt of the Earth's axis is inclined neither away from nor towards the Sun, causing the center of the solar disk to lie perfectly on the celestial equator, yielding roughly equal lengths of day and night globally.

AAU_midterm_2023.subject: Geography
AAU_midterm_2023.text: 70. _______________ is a census undertaking approach where each individual is recorded at the place where he/she was found at the time of the census. (2023)
AAU_midterm_2023.explanation: A de facto census records people exactly where they are physically present on the designated census night, regardless of whether that location is their permanent residence. This is distinguished from a de jure census, which records individuals based on their legal or usual address.
